headline: OpenAI's AI resolves over 100 open math problems as it forms new advisory group
summary: OpenAI has established an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence to bridge with the mathematical community, following claims its AI solved over 100 open math problems.
details: On Monday, OpenAI announced a new independent advisory group, the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. This group aims to give mathematicians more input into the company’s math-oriented research. OpenAI also claims its internal model has resolved over 100 additional open problems across most areas of mathematics.

This announcement follows the abrupt publication of a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem by OpenAI's AI. Many prominent mathematicians have expressed concerns about the rapid pace of these results, with 25 Fields Medalists signing an open letter regarding AI labs' impact on their intellectual work.

The new group will primarily serve in an advisory capacity, assessing the significance of new results and coordinating their release. Members, who won't be paid, can offer unsolicited advice, go public with their views, and control their own membership, ensuring a degree of independence from OpenAI.

However, the group will not have the authority to slow down or redirect OpenAI’s ongoing mathematical research. The Institute for Advanced Study emphasized that while they give advice, they lack decision-making power at any AI company, with responsibility resting solely with the company.

Nine prominent mathematicians have been named as initial members of the group. Notably, only one of these members, IAS’s Camillo De Lellis, also signed the Fields Medalists’ letter expressing concerns about AI in mathematics.
